narrative.overview:
Orbi OS is a small desktop environment — a drawn orbital field, an application dock, windows that move — that carries a working developer portfolio inside it. The visitor is not scrolling a page; they are opening applications.

The thesis the build holds itself to: the desktop is a precision orbital instrument — one luminous body at the focus of one drawn trajectory — refusing the space-UI default of scattered stars and neon gradients. The proportion: 70% professional work, 20% exploration, 10% experiment. The window manager is the stage, never the subject. If an interaction does not help someone read the work, it does not ship.

The first viewport is the whole thesis in one frame: a full-bleed orbital field; the emblem centred at ~62vw with the orbit crossing the sphere; orbiOS thin and wide under it; "— Desktop Environment —" beneath; project apps filed in the left column; the glass dock at the foot; the status pill top right.
keyCharacteristics: Obsidian field, blue-silver volumetric light, hairline trajectories, a rim-lit sphere, ultra-thin tracked type, one signal-green status.
Two themes inverted on one set of variables; the emblem carries its own second lighting of the same palette.
One mark everywhere — "the apogee": a core at the orbit's focus, a tilted orbit in two arcs, one accent satellite. Drawn in currentColor so both themes get it for free.
One distant trajectory crosses the emblem's sphere on purpose: a 1px hairline at 0.22 opacity, rotated 14°, breaking the silhouette so the diagram reads through the body.
Hairline borders instead of shadows; one soft shadow under a window, the dock, and the menus.
Radii 6–18px, pills for chips. Motion 180–320ms on interactions; slow ambient clocks from 8s to 131s; nothing at all under prefers-reduced-motion.
Geist for the interface, Geist Mono for labels, metadata, terminals and code.
Every number comes from src/data/github.json or src/data/site.config.ts.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent says "this is active". It never fills a large region, and it never competes with the content of an application.

rules.name: The Glow Rule
rules.body: A glow marks a light source or a live state — the emblem's halo, the signal dot, the open-app dot, the boot bar — never a surface, never text, never a border at rest.

rules.name: The Tracking Rule
rules.body: The wordmark is the one sans line allowed wide tracking; every other wide-tracked line is mono. Titles carry negative tracking instead. One element never carries both.

dos: Do keep a window's state in the manager and its content in the app.
Do seat a new window inside the desktop; never let it open off-screen.
Do give an address to what a visitor might send: #/projects/<name> opens the system at that project.
Do keep the accent for active state and the signal for live state.
Do draw the mark from Mark and the scene from Emblem, never a second SVG or a glyph stand-in.
Do tune the boot by BOOT_MS and the project load by PROJECT_LOAD_MS, not by editing the beats.
Do keep the trajectories hairlines (≤12% ink or accent) and the stars few and placed.
Do keep every sequence cancellable — the boot skips on input, the terminal lands on the first wheel, key or tap.
Do keep the parallax to a few pixels across its three depths.
Do keep the no-script document in step with the applications.
donts: Don't scatter stars, run neon gradients, or take the space-UI default: one luminous body at the focus of one drawn trajectory is the whole thesis.
Don't put a glow on anything that is not a light source or a live state.
Don't add a third accent, or let the accent fill a large region.
Don't animate the wordmark's tracking outside the boot, or move the welcome lockup: windows cover it, never shift it.
Don't copy Windows, macOS or a Linux desktop: the shell has its own status pill, its own dock and its own orbital field.
Don't invent metrics, uptime, counters or experience. The numbers are the committed snapshot.
Don't let the system be the subject: the windows are where the work is.
Don't ship an interaction that does not help the work be read.
